title: Spirits at a glance
lead: Every spirit on the back bar, in a sentence or two: what it’s made from and the words guests use.

sections.name: Clear spirits

lines.label: In short
lines.text: Vodka, gin, blanco tequila and white rum.

know: Vodka is clean and neutral, from any farm base.
Gin is a neutral spirit where juniper leads.
Blanco tequila and white rum are clear because they’re unaged or barely aged.
sections.source: EU spirit drinks regulation 2019/787, Annex I (eur-lex.europa.eu); Mexican tequila standard NOM-006-SCFI (as summarized by Difford’s Guide)

sections.name: Whiskey

lines.label: In short
lines.text: Grain, distilled, then aged in wood.

know: Bourbon is at least 51% corn, aged in new charred oak.
Rye is at least 51% rye: drier and spicier.
Scotch is made in Scotland and aged at least three years.
sections.source: US TTB standards of identity, 27 CFR 5.143 (law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/27/5.143); Scotch Whisky Regulations 2009 (legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2009/2890)

sections.name: Agave and cane

lines.label: In short
lines.text: Tequila and mezcal from agave, rum from sugarcane.

know: Tequila is blue agave, from Mexico.
Mezcal can use other agaves and is often smoky.
Rum is sugarcane: molasses or fresh juice.
sections.source: Mexican tequila standard NOM-006-SCFI (as summarized by Difford’s Guide); EU spirit drinks regulation 2019/787, Annex I (eur-lex.europa.eu)

sections.name: Brandy, liqueurs and vermouth

lines.label: In short
lines.text: Brandy from fruit, liqueurs sweet, vermouth is wine.

know: Brandy is distilled from wine or fruit. Cognac is France’s.
A liqueur is a spirit with sugar and flavor added.
Vermouth is fortified wine: fridge once open.
sections.source: EU spirit drinks regulation 2019/787, Annex I (eur-lex.europa.eu); BNIC rules for Cognac (as summarized on Wikipedia); Common bar practice

video.title: Bartending Class 101: Vodka and Gin (How to be a Bartender)

keyPoints.line: is clean and neutral, from any farm base.
is a neutral spirit where juniper leads.
tequila is unaged or rested under two months.
is light and mixes like vodka with a touch of sweetness.

read.where: Most clear spirits never sit in a barrel, so they taste of what they’re made from. **Vodka** is meant to taste of almost nothing. **Gin** is neutral spirit flavored with botanicals, and **juniper** has to lead. **Blanco tequila** tastes of agave. **White rum** tastes of cane.

stops.name: Vodka
stops.text: Clean. From wheat, rye, potato or corn.

read.mixup: A **citrus vodka** isn’t a gin. Gin has to taste of **juniper** first.
read.sayIt: Do you have a vodka you like, or should I suggest one?

video.title: Bartender's Guide to Whiskey and Rum 101 (Everything you ever wanted to know)

keyPoints.line: is grain, distilled, then aged in wood.
is at least 51% corn: rounder and sweeter.
is at least 51% rye: drier and spicier.
is made in Scotland. Some are smoky.

read.bigIdea: All whiskey is grain and wood. The grain and the place change the taste.
read.where: Whiskey starts as a beer made from grain, gets distilled, then ages in oak, which gives it its color and vanilla. **Bourbon** is American, at least **51% corn**, aged in **new charred oak**. **Rye** is at least **51% rye**. **Scotch** has to be made in **Scotland** and aged at least **three years**.
read.mixup: **Bourbon** and **rye** are both American. The grain is the difference: corn is sweeter, rye is spicier.
read.sayIt: Do you like it sweeter, like a bourbon, or spicier, like a rye?

video.title: Mezcal vs Tequila - What You're Getting Wrong About These Spirits

keyPoints.line: is agave too, often smoky from pit roasting.
is sugarcane: molasses or fresh juice.
blanco → reposado → añejo: more oak, more vanilla.

read.bigIdea: Agave makes tequila and mezcal. Sugarcane makes rum.
read.where: **Tequila** is made from **blue agave** in Mexico. It’s sold by age: **blanco** (unaged or under two months), **reposado** (rested at least **two months**) and **añejo** (at least **a year**). **Mezcal** can use other agaves and is often **smoky**, because the agave is roasted in pits. **Rum** is distilled from **sugarcane**, usually molasses, sometimes fresh juice.

stops.name: Añejo
stops.text: A **year** or more: vanilla and caramel.

read.mixup: **Mezcal** isn’t a kind of tequila with a worm. It’s its own agave spirit, and the smoke comes from roasting.
read.sayIt: Would you like it smoky? Try it with mezcal.

keyPoints.line: is distilled from wine or fruit.
is a spirit with sugar and flavor added.
is fortified wine. Fridge once open.

read.bigIdea: The bottles that finish a drink.
read.where: **Brandy** is distilled from **wine or fruit**; **Cognac** is the famous one, from France. A **liqueur** is a spirit with **sugar and flavor** added: orange, coffee, herbal, nut. **Vermouth** is **wine** flavored with herbs and fortified, so once it’s open it goes in the **fridge**.
read.mixup: **Vermouth** isn’t a spirit. It’s wine, so it spoils like wine.
read.sayIt: Something after dinner? A Cognac, or an amaro?

sources: EU spirit drinks regulation 2019/787, Annex I (eur-lex.europa.eu); US TTB standards of identity, 27 CFR 5.143 (law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/27/5.143); Scotch Whisky Regulations 2009 (legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2009/2890); Mexican tequila standard NOM-006-SCFI (as summarized by Difford’s Guide); BNIC rules for Cognac (as summarized on Wikipedia). Facts taken from the Level 2 lessons, which cite them. Nov 8, 2026.
